### A Necrotizing Enterocolitis Form Meets Neither Definition {#sec-problem-details-36}

The NeoIPC Surveillance Protocol defines necrotizing enterocolitis in two ways: symptom-based, by at least one radiological sign together with at least one clinical sign, or surgical, by at least one surgical or pathological finding.
When a necrotizing enterocolitis form is completed, the platform checks it against these definitions and refuses to complete it if it meets neither.
A completed form that meets neither has therefore reached the platform around this check, for example through an import, completed before the check existed, or changed after it was completed.
This message appears in the validation report when a completed necrotizing enterocolitis form records neither a radiological and a clinical sign nor a surgical or pathological finding; the message gives the number of each the form records.

Please open the form (see @sec-solution-15), reopen it for editing (see @sec-solution-9), check its findings against the definitions, and complete it again (see @sec-solution-8), which makes the platform check them again.
If the infection meets neither definition, it cannot be recorded as necrotizing enterocolitis; please delete the form in that case (see @sec-solution-12).
